body:
Minutes:

- Form Attribute Element Reflection: Luke proposed adding element reflection for the form attribute to address missing functionality, such as referencing forms in parent trees that current reference target mechanisms cannot reach ([00:04:25](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.ewlat83nv86x)). The current approach, used by libraries like Shoelace, involves intercepting click events and calling request submit, but this fails to trigger behaviors like the default pseudo-class or proper submitter association. The proposed solution involves adding a setter to the form property to enable element reflection, and the participants discussed the technical viability of this approach ([00:05:52](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.2k7ra5yujwhw)).
- Shadow DOM and Form Association Challenges: The participants debated the feasibility of setting form associations across shadow boundaries ([00:08:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.c3ebyol6c9s1)). Luke noted current limitations where element reflection properties prevent setting values to elements inside shadow roots that are not at the same level or an ancestor level, causing potential issues for custom elements ([00:10:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.kwrgm4gnq8t0)). Jake Archibald and Olli Pettay questioned the necessity of these encapsulation constraints, arguing they do not align with how JavaScript access currently works ([00:11:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.i0m3wrhgl07v)) ([00:15:19](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.oyboyoew7ner)). The group agreed to leave this as an open issue to investigate whether existing implementations enforce these checks, and Luke offered to create a prototype to test the behavior ([00:13:11](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.tailhvhqtx0a)) ([00:15:19](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.oyboyoew7ner)).
- Responsive Iframe Resizing Proposal: Koji Ishii provided an update on the responsive iframe feature, which resizes iframes based on content size, requiring opt-ins from both the parent and child via a cascading style sheets property and a meta tag ([00:18:43](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.aa07c659n9qn)). The feature requires immutability once active for security reasons, and recent updates to the pull request now require declaring the embedding parent's origin ([00:20:43](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.5ukus63i26af)). Simon Pieters raised concerns regarding how to detect the rendering state, noting that checking for a body or frame set element may not cover edge cases like scalable vector graphics documents. The participants concluded that checking the reveal steps is a more robust method for ensuring the feature's immutability ([00:22:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.1se2gf1p4mw5)) ([00:25:31](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.9yrbpw567d6y)).
- Iframe Navigation and Layout Reset: The group discussed the necessity of triggering a reset of the locked embedded size when an iframe is navigated, ensuring that the new document does not receive the previous size information ([00:28:56](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.mmg22f8hefog)). Koji Ishii stated that the current recommendation is to reset to a default size of 300 by 150 pixels ([00:30:56](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.o2jxk9pxfil9)). Koji Ishii will investigate the HTML navigation algorithm to determine the precise timing for this reset to ensure it is correctly specified ([00:28:56](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.mmg22f8hefog)).
- Responsive Iframe Security and Referral Policy: Simon Pieters expressed concerns that a strict referral policy, which hides the origin, could conflict with the responsive iframe feature and potentially allow a child iframe to guess the parent's origin ([00:32:52](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.kiqj8mv6hegb)). The participants discussed whether to restrict the feature when a strict referral policy is present. They reached a consensus that they could restrict the feature if a referral policy is set to hide the origin, though they may allow it if the policy is set to star, and they considered whether to include a warning in the specification instead ([00:36:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.q2ft8xw5mea3)).
- Sanitizer API Development and Trusted Types: Noam Rosenthal provided an update on the Sanitizer API (issue #11669), noting that a stack of pull requests has been posted. The participants discussed the handling of trusted types with mixed extensible markup language and hypertext markup language content, which currently causes errors ([00:39:15](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.gxmi3tgiz9dg)). They agreed to explore passing document type context as a parameter to resolve these trusted types issues ([00:41:24](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.bts3mlvpu688)). Jake Archibald noted that the Sanitizer API logic appeared reasonable, and they identified that the parser's attribute-merging behavior for the body element requires careful sanitization ([00:44:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.qevh67vch016)). The group agreed to label the issue as stage two while planning to look into stage three in the future ([00:46:56](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.3aqooqr56aaj)).
- Web Speech API Text Tracks: Paul Adenot highlighted the importance of the Web Speech API's ability to add or remove text tracks dynamically, specifically for low-latency auto-generation of tracks when switching audio streams. This functionality is becoming increasingly important as the API moves toward shipping, and there was general support for the proposal to add this capability ([00:48:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W-hhZyYdzV41kIvd9EWWLhWddj6wZzA_Ct7Ky8xojDc/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-8OvIAfPJfjxYE6jDykzcXg&tab=t.4iz6vv7dqk15#heading=h.uod6gb3bxsbb)).
